taxonomyNote: Formerly in genus Eumeces; NatureServe notes disagreement over whether the southern subspecies is E. m. epipleurotus or E. m. gaigeae.
fieldMarks: Smooth, glossy scales and short fore and hind limbs; total length 10.2-19.4 cm.
Multiple stripes down the body alternating light and dark on a dark brown to olive-green base.
A pair of white stripes on the third scale row from the middle of the back.
behavior: Diurnal; active about April to early October (March-October in the north of the range), with crepuscular activity in hot weather.
Secretive; usually found under ground cover such as rocks, logs and cow dung; overwinters underground.
Lays 2-9 eggs in spring; the female attends the eggs.
habitat: Northern populations: short- and mixed-grass prairie and sandhills on sandy or loose soil.
Southern populations: desert, streamside thickets, pinyon-juniper and pine-oak woodland, fir forest and shrublands.
range: Southern South Dakota, Nebraska, southeastern Wyoming and northeastern Colorado (northern segment); southern Colorado, southeastern Utah, Arizona, New Mexico and western Texas (southern segment); roughly 910-2,620 m. Not found in Canada.
